outcome.description: the fundamental id this verdict is for, e.g. O1

magnitude.description: how big; MUST be 'n/a' iff direction is 'too-uncertain'

time_horizon.description: when felt; MUST be 'n/a' iff direction is 'too-uncertain'

plain.description: 1-2 sentence plain-English summary at ~age-12 reading level: the gist + the main caveat

biggest_unknown.description: one sentence — the main caveat / what would change the verdict

claims.description: the EVIDENCE-BOUND factual backbone. Every factual assertion the verdict rests on is one claim, each tied to a provided evidence unit and quoting a verbatim span from that unit's snippet. Assert NOTHING you cannot bind to an evidence quote.

tier.description: stated = what the policy promises (cite evidence unit 'M', the manifesto); measurable = current sourced baseline; projected = contested forecast

claim.description: the factual statement, in plain words

evidence_id.description: the id of the provided evidence unit that backs this claim (e.g. 'M' for the policy's own text, or 'E3')

quote.description: a VERBATIM span copied from that evidence unit's snippet that supports the claim. Must appear word-for-word in the snippet.

rationale.description: the reasoning that connects the claims to the direction/magnitude verdict, in plain English. Interpretation only — every FACT it uses must already be a claim above. Concise (~300 words).

time_split.description: OPTIONAL. Only for dual_horizon outcomes (O6, O12, O13) AND only when the near-term and long-term effects point MATERIALLY DIFFERENT ways (e.g. cost now, gain later). Omit entirely otherwise. The top-level `direction` remains the overall verdict; this just surfaces the divergence for display.

near_direction.description: the effect felt in the near term (this parliament)

long_direction.description: the effect over the long term (~10yr+)

note.description: one line: why near and long diverge
